Our method leverages a downsampled global mosaic to guide local blending, eliminating the need to load the full-resolution dataset into memory. We further introduce two adaptive execution strategies that vary the number of solver iterations per tile, improving both efficiency and quality. We demonstrate our approach using large orthomosaic datasets from the National Ecological Observatory Network (NEON), and implement the pipeline using the SYCL programming model for cross-platform portability.

title: Supervised Learning of Wireless Signal Waveforms in the Era of Radar-Communications Convergence
abstract: Widely recognized as a candidate technology for 6G, joint communication and sensing (JCAS) is expected to enable a range of emerging applications in wireless networks. However, incorporating radio sensing capabilities introduces new design challenges and demands novel approaches across various research and engineering disciplines. This paper studies the waveform classification task not only for dedicated communication and radar but also for fully integrated JCAS waveforms. To this end, we generate wireless waveforms that belong to eight classes, including four pure communications standard signal waveforms, two classical radar waveforms, and two fully integrated JCAS candidate waveforms. We examine the dataset's statistical properties and evaluate several machine learning and deep learning classifiers based on expert feature extraction and raw data. Numerical simulations show that expert feature-based classifiers exhibit limited accuracy for the considered task, even for a very high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). The classifier that learns from raw data yields high accuracy, but requires either a high-performance computing platform or further architectural optimization to meet real-time requirements. Additionally, we investigate the complexity, inference time, and memory footprint of the designed classifiers in the context of their practical implementation in wireless communication systems.

title: Welcoming Remarks
abstract: I am honoured to welcome everyone to the Namibia University of Science and Technology (NUST) for the 5th International Conference on Emerging Trends in Networks and Computer Communications (ETNCC). This hybrid event is scheduled to take place from August 5 to 7, 2025, and is organised by the UNESCO Chair on Secure High-Performance Computing for Higher Education and Research within NUST's Faculty of Computing and Informatics, under the leadership of Prof. Dharm Singh Jat. The conference is technically co-sponsored by the IEEE South Africa Section and is supported by IEEE Region 8. This platform provides a truly unique and invaluable opportunity for us to come together-bringing diverse perspectives, expertise, and passion to collaboratively shape the future of sustainable development. By fostering innovation, dialogue, and shared commitment, we can drive meaningful progress toward creating a more equitable, resilient, and environmentally responsible world for generations to come.

title: The Hidden Variables in the Future of Quantum Computing in 6G
abstract: 5G has been commercialised and 6G standardisation has just started. The vision of these networks are going to pose unprecedented computing challenges on the infrastructure. To ensure the computing infrastructure is capable to assure the necessary promises, integration between `classical' and quantum computing has started being researched by the industrial and scientific communities in cloud computing scenarios. In the years, various technologies for quantum computing have been developed with different performances and characteristics. Superconducting and trapped-ions have been attracting a lot of attention and investments. That mainly due to the best fidelities, gate times, for the number of computational qubits offered. These quantum computing technologies work at very low temperatures (below some Kelvins) and require cryogenics. Nevertheless, in the history, the success of ICT technologies has also passed through their flexibility, sustainability (e.g., energy usage, cost, scalability). Current cryogenic methods for quantum computing face significant sustainability challenges due to their extreme energy demands and reliance on finite resources. The cooling infrastructure represents one of the most significant sustainability challenge in quantum computing. That is why other solutions like photonic and NV-centre diamond-based quantum computing could offer a suitable alternative to match the requirements of future generation networks.

title: Carbon-Aware Computing: Redesigning Algorithms for a Greener Future
abstract: The rise in computational pressure in the data centers, cloud, and edge has resulted in rising energy and carbon footprint. Although much focus has been on hardware efficiency and the use of renewable energy, algorithmic redesign is a close and highly effective way of looking at sustainability. In this paper, carbon-conscious computing gets reviewed with special reference to the alcoholic approaches to workload scheduling, offloading tasks, resource provisioning, and carbon footprint estimation. The most notable case studies are Google carbon-intelligent workload management, GreenScale edge-cloud scheduling, CASPER distributed web-service provisioning, market-driven edge AI optimization and the Green Algorithms footprint analysis tool. These approaches prove to have the ability to reduce emissions by up to 70 percent without affecting performance, latency, and cost. Other challenges that have been pointed out in the study include challenges in intermittency of renewable energy, computational overhead, and lack of standardized carbon measures. The future of the AI-based scheduling is predictive, further combination with the carbon markets, and cross-layer optimization of devices, edge, and data center. Carbon aware redesigning of algorithms is depicted as an important move towards making computing systems greener and more sustainable.

title: AIML-based Pest Detection using Hyperspectral Imaging and Edge Inference in 6G Farms
abstract: The rapid development of intelligent agriculture is associated with the necessity of sophisticated, scalable, and real-time pest detection solutions to guarantee the health of crops and food security. In this work, the authors suggest a framework of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AIML)-based technology, using hyperspectral imaging and edge inference to be used in the new 6G farm ecosystem. Hyperspectral imaging has fine-grained spectral characteristics, which allow early and accurate discrimination of normal and pest crops. These multidimensional datasets are fed on to optimized AIML models, such as deep neural networks optimized on spectral-spatial feature extraction. In order to circumvent latency and bandwidth issues that are common with transmitting hyperspectral data to centralized servers, inference is executed at the edge based on low-power, high-performance computing nodes deployed in 6G-enabled farm infrastructures. The combination of edge computing and 6G ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) will provide real-time detection, and distributed learning methods will guarantee the flexibility of the models to operate in the variety of agricultural conditions. The results of experimental validation in simulated 6G farm testbeds reveal that there is a substantial enhancement in detection accuracy, response time and scalability in comparison with traditional pest monitoring systems. The presented strategy reflects on the revolutionary impact of hyperspectral-AIML-edge integration in the next-generation, precision agriculture, which is going to provide the path to sustainable, resilient, and intelligent farming.

title: Towards Affordable, Adaptive and Automatic GNN Training on CPU-GPU Heterogeneous Platforms
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have been widely adopted due to their strong performance. However, GNN training often relies on expensive, high-performance computing platforms, limiting accessibility for many tasks. Profiling of representative GNN workloads indicates that substantial efficiency gains are possible on resource-constrained devices by fully exploiting available resources. This paper introduces $\mathrmA^3 \textGNN$, a framework for Affordable, Adaptive, and Automatic GNN training on heterogeneous CPU-GPU platforms. It improves resource usage through locality-aware sampling and fine-grained parallelism scheduling. Moreover, it leverages reinforcement learning to explore the design space and achieve pareto-optimal trade-offs among throughput, memory footprint, and accuracy. Experiments show that $\mathrmA^3$ GNN can bridge the performance gap, allowing seven Nvidia 2080Ti GPUs to outperform two A100 GPUs by up to $1.8 \times$ in throughput with minimal accuracy loss.

title: Coordinating Artificial Intelligence and Bitcoin Mining Workloads: A Risk-Aware Distributional Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Approach
abstract: The rapid expansion of Artificial Intelligence (AI) workloads has created substantial energy requirements for contemporary data centers, which generate worries about infrastructure expansion and operational expenses and environmental sustainability. The worldwide shift toward renewable energy creates uncertainties in power supply that lead to grid instability and energy curtailment problems. This paper explores the synergistic convergence of AI compute infrastructure and Bitcoin (BTC) mining as a novel, energy-aware co-optimization framework. We propose a Distributional Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) system that dynamically allocates surplus energy between latency-sensitive AI jobs and highly flexible BTC mining operations. The proposed solution includes essential participants like renewable energy producers, energy management agents, AI clusters and BTC miners operating within a centralized training and decentralized execution paradigm. The simulation demonstrates that our MARL-driven methodology reduces the reduction in renewable energy by up to 65 \% while maintaining high BTC mining profitability and stable grid demand and ensuring AI service level compliance. These findings suggest a path toward sustainable, intelligent energy computation ecosystems where AI and blockchain technologies operate not as competitors, but as complementary agents within a unified infrastructure.

title: Exploring Time Predictability for High-Bandwidth Memory Technology
abstract: High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) is a 3D-stacked DRAM interface standard that provides higher bandwidth, lower power consumption, and a smaller footprint than DDR4 and GDDR5. It is increasingly adopted in supercomputers, datacenters, and high-end embedded platforms, such as autonomous driving systems, where it meets the performance demands of artificial intelligence and other data-intensive workloads. Beyond raw performance, many of these applications require deterministic or bounded response times, either for hard real-time safety-critical systems or to provide Quality-of-Service (QoS) guarantees in multi-tenant HPC, datacenter, and cloud environments. While performance predictability has been extensively studied for DDR memory controllers, it remains largely unexplored for HBM. Although HBM shares some characteristics with DDR, such as command reordering to reduce data bus reversals, it introduces additional challenges, including stricter timing constraints that increase command latency within bank groups. In this work, we propose an implementable architectural model of a deterministic HBM controller that addresses these challenges, together with a quantitative closed-form analysis to fully characterize its response times. We present a complete physical implementation derived from the model and describe practical simulation and synthesis toolflows enabling extensive experimental evaluation with real-world memory-intensive workloads, also including aspects such as the impact of address-to-bank/row/column mapping on HBM command performance. The proposed controller achieves a peak throughput of 13.5 GB/s per pseudo-channel and an aggregate peak throughput of 432 GB/s while providing time predictability guarantees.

title: Retrospective on the Lax Report: Then and Now
abstract: More than four decades after its release, the 1982 Lax Report remains a landmark blueprint for U.S. high-performance computing (HPC) policy. This retrospective revisits the report's four principal recommendations, evaluating each on its current fulfillment. While the HPC ecosystem has matured through network advances, broader access, and the integration of AI and distributed computing, gaps in workforce development, scientific software sustainability, and architectural innovation tailored to science needs remain. This article traces HPC's evolution from centralized supercomputers to today's cloud-augmented, AI-converged landscape and highlights how market-driven hardware design increasingly diverges from the needs of rigorous scientific computing. The paper also calls for sustained public investment in hardware-software co-design, workforce pipelines, and open, science-centered infrastructure.

title: Optimizing Management of Persistent Data Structures in High-Performance Analytics
abstract: Large-scale data analytics workflows ingest massive input data into various data structures, including graphs and key-value datastores. These data structures undergo multiple transformations and computations and are typically reused in incremental and iterative analytics workflows. Persisting in-memory views of these data structures enables reusing them beyond the scope of a single program run while avoiding repetitive raw data ingestion overheads. Memory-mapped I/O enables persisting in-memory data structures without data serialization and deserialization overheads. However, memory-mapped I/O lacks the key feature of persisting consistent snapshots of these data structures for incremental ingestion and processing. The obstacles to efficient virtual memory snapshots using memory-mapped I/O include background writebacks outside the application's control, and the significantly high storage footprint of such snapshots. To address these limitations, we present Privateer, a memory and storage management tool that enables storage-efficient virtual memory snapshotting while also optimizing snapshot I/O performance. We integrated Privateer into Metall, a state-of-the-art persistent memory allocator for C++, and the Lightning Memory-Mapped Database (LMDB), a widely-used key-value datastore in data analytics and machine learning. Privateer optimized application performance by 1.22\texttimes when storing data structure snapshots to node-local storage, and up to 16.7\texttimes when storing snapshots to a parallel file system. Privateer also optimizes storage efficiency of incremental data structure snapshots by up to 11\texttimes using data deduplication and compression.

title: Bridging the Gap between Academic Curricula and Industry Requirements through Faculty Industry Internships
abstract: The persistent disconnect between academic curricula and industry requirements remains a critical challenge in higher education, particularly in fast-evolving fields such as artificial intelligence (AI), semiconductor technology, and cyber security. This paper proposes faculty industry internships as a transformative mechanism to align academic training with industry needs. By immersing faculty in industry environments, these programs empower educators to acquire practical skills, integrate real-world insights into teaching, and mentor students effectively. Case studies from Indian institutions like IISc Bengaluru and C-DAC demonstrate the success of Faculty Development Programs (FDPs) in fostering industry-relevant competencies, while empirical data from a mixed-methods study involving 150 faculty members and 30 industry experts highlight improved curriculum alignment and student employability. Challenges such as faculty resistance and funding constraints are addressed through hybrid models and policy reforms like the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020. The paper concludes with actionable strategies for institutions and policymakers to prioritize faculty-industry collaboration, ensuring the sustainability and relevance of technical education in India.

title: The Challenges of Setting up Sustainable Research Data Infrastructure
abstract: Research project setups in academia usually do not outlive the end of the project. This is even more prominent for academic projects that deal with research data infrastructure. To address this the High-Performance Computing Center Stuttgart (HLRS) is looking at a sustainable approach to operate research data infrastructure. At its core this approach consists of building up a dedicated platform. The overall goal is to benefit from synergy effects by having services of multiple projects sharing the same hardware platform thereby reducing project costs, as well as to accumulate experience from different projects regarding research data management and research data infrastructure within one comprehensive team.

title: Energy-Efficient and Balanced Cloud Task Scheduling Using Lion Optimization Algorithm with Elite Opposition-Based Learning
abstract: Cloud computing has emerged as a vital technology for providing scalable and flexible access to computing resources. With the increasing demand for cloud services, efficient task scheduling has become critical to ensure optimal performance, balanced resource utilization, and reduced energy consumption. This study proposes the integration of the Lion Optimization Algorithm (LOA) with Elite Opposition-Based Learning (EOBL) to improve task scheduling in cloud computing environments. The simulation was conducted using CloudSim, configured with $\mathbf5 4$ virtual machines, 18 hosts, and 6 datacenters. Three datasets were employed: the San Diego Supercomputer Center (SDSC) Blue Horizon logs, a simple random dataset, and a stratified random dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that LOA outperforms the Genetic Algorithm (GA) in several parameters, including average execution time and imbalance degree. Furthermore, the hybrid LOA-EOBL significantly enhances scheduling performance across multiple criteria, such as makespan, total wait time, average start and finish times, scheduling length, throughput, resource utilization, and energy consumption. The improvements are consistent across all datasets, with notable advantages observed in complex workloads represented by the SDSC dataset. These findings highlight the potential of LOA-EOBL as an effective hybrid optimization method for cloud task scheduling, offering improvements in efficiency, fairness, and sustainability compared to traditional approaches.

title: Opportunities for Advanced Logic Technology with Dual-sided Integrations: From Lateral to Vertical Transistors
abstract: With the great advancement of semiconductor processes, the CMOS integration on both sides of wafer provides brand new scope for advanced logic technologies by fully utilizing the wafer backside, emerging as one of the key knobs to further extend the Moore's law. Benefited from it, lateral transport transistors can be stacked in a back-to-back fashion to form the Flip FET (FFET), doubling the transistor density. Furthermore, similar concepts can be applied to vertical transistors to realize the dual-sided vertical FET (DSVFET), with better device symmetry and area efficiency. In this work, we systematically reviewed the applications of dual-sided integration for advanced logic devices, from the lateral transistors to the vertical ones. Specifically, to meet the urgent requirement of high energy efficiency computing (EEC) for future AI applications, the DSVFET was thoroughly investigated in terms of process development, electrical characteristics, circuit design and chip-level evaluation. Thanks to the adjustable vertical structure, DSVFET holds great features of both reduced parasitic and area. Area scalability of DSVFET is also confirmed at standard cell (~30\%) and block (~40\%) level. The block level evaluation validates the energy efficiency benefit of DSVFET at nominal Vdd range of EEC by ~15\% energy delay product gain. This work validates the great potential of dual-sided integration in the next-generation logic technology.

title: Poster: Evaluation of x86 and ARM Energy Efficiency for 5G Open RAN Deployment
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of the energy consumption of x86 and ARM processors running an opensource 5G Open RAN protocol stack. Tests were conducted across multiple high-performance processing platforms to evaluate power consumption under different network scenarios, including traffic and multiple users. Results show a clear distinction between x86 and ARM platforms, where the latter consistently demonstrates superior energy efficiency, reaching up to twice the performance-per-watt of x86 platforms in uplink-heavy workloads with multiple users. These findings highlight ARM's potential as a powerefficient alternative for 5G Open RAN deployments, particularly in energy-constrained environments.

title: Optimizing Methane Detection On Board Satellites: Speed, Accuracy, and Low-Power Solutions for Resource-Constrained Hardware
abstract: Methane is a potent greenhouse gas, and detecting its leaks early via hyperspectral satellite imagery can help mitigate climate change. Meanwhile, many existing missions operate in manual tasking regimes only, thus missing potential events of interest. To overcome slow downlink rates costeffectively, onboard detection is a viable solution. However, traditional methane enhancement methods are too computationally demanding for resource-limited onboard hardware. This work accelerates methane detection by focusing on efficient, low-power algorithms. We test fast target detection methods (ACE, CEM) that have not been previously used for methane detection and propose a Mag1c-SAS – a significantly faster variant of the current state-of-the-art algorithm for methane detection: Mag1c. To explore their true detection potential, we integrate them with a machine learning model (U-Net, LinkNet). Our results identify two promising candidates (Mag1c-SAS and CEM), both acceptably accurate for the detection of strong plumes and computationally efficient enough for onboard deployment: one optimized more for accuracy, the other more for speed, achieving up to ~100\texttimes and ~230\texttimes faster computation than original Mag1c on resource-limited hardware. Additionally, we propose and evaluate three band selection strategies. One of them can outperform the method traditionally used in the field while using fewer channels, leading to even faster processing without compromising accuracy. This research lays the foundation for future advancements in onboard methane detection with minimal hardware requirements, improving timely data delivery. The produced code, data, and models are open-sourced and can be accessed from https://github.com/zaitra/methane-filters-benchmark.

title: A Multi-Level Software Supply Chain Security Defense System for Cloud-Native and High-Performance Computing Environments
abstract: With the acceleration of the digital process, the software supply chain has become a key target of cyber attacks, and its security defense is facing severe challenges. This paper proposes to build a full-chain and multi-level security defense system for the software supply chain. By analyzing the security risks in each link of the full life cycle of software (development, construction, distribution, deployment, operation and maintenance), the paper systematically expounds the construction path of the defense system from three dimensions: technical defense, management mechanism and external collaboration. The research shows that embedding security into all links of the full life cycle, combined with SBOM-based technical tools, standardized management processes and ecological collaboration mechanisms, can realize the transformation from "passive response" to "active defense", providing a comprehensive solution for resisting supply chain attacks. This framework is particularly applicable to cloud-native CI/CD pipelines and high-performance computing environments, where distributed software components and large-scale deployment increase the complexity and risk of supply chain attacks.

title: Evolution of Parameter Uncertainties in Semi-empirical Mass Formula Based on High-performance Computing Potential-Energy-Surface Calculations for Even-even Rare-earth Nuclei
abstract: High-performance computing (HPC) and parallel computing techniques are employed to systematically derive the microscopic component energies of 763 even-even nuclei based on the Potential-Energy-Surface (PES) approach. Nuclear masses of even-even rare-earth nuclei are analyzed. The coefficients of the semi-empirical mass formula are determined via Gaussian elimination and least-squares fitting. Monte Carlo techniques are employed to quantify parameter uncertainties by sampling a large dataset. Experimental binding energy errors are incorporated into the analysis. New parameters for the phenomenological Bethe-Weizs\"acker mass formula are presented, including their uncertainties and Pearson correlation coefficients. The results demonstrate enhanced universality of the theoretical parameters derived from experimental data in the rare-earth region, achieving a root-mean-square (r.m.s.) deviation of 0.3679 MeV. Our findings show that experimental binding energy errors strongly affect model parameter uncertainties. Variations in experimental error propagate proportionally to theoretical parameter uncertainties. However, the effect on the Pearson correlation coefficients among the parameters remains minimal. Therefore, it is advisable to account for parameter correlations to reduce the errors of the theoretical model. This work demonstrates HPC's effectiveness in large-scale nuclear physics data processing, offering an interdisciplinary paradigm integrating parallel computing with complex physical modeling. It expands HPC's application scope in microscopic nuclear research and provides valuable technical insights for cross-domain computational methodologies.

title: Balancing Performance and Sustainability: A Review of Energy-Aware Scheduling in HPC
abstract: Energy efficiency has become a critical design priority in high-performance computing (HPC), where the scale and complexity of modern systems amplify the trade-off between computational performance and sustainability. Traditional job scheduling strategies have primarily emphasized throughput and fairness, but the growing demands of exascale-class architectures require methods that also minimize energy consumption while maintaining high utilization. Recent research has introduced a wide spectrum of energy-aware scheduling approaches, ranging from heuristic extensions and Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS) models to reinforcement learning and machine learning-driven frameworks. This paper provides a structured synthesis of these approaches, categorizing them into heuristic-based methods, DVFS and analytical models, reinforcement learning schedulers, prediction-augmented strategies, and machine learning-based resource mapping. Each category is examined with respect to methodological design, datasets, evaluation metrics, and comparative performance. Key challenges are identified, including scalability in heterogeneous environments, reproducibility of AI-driven approaches, and prediction uncertainty. To capture the progression of ideas, we present a timeline of advancements and a clustered taxonomy of scheduling paradigms. Finally, the paper outlines future research directions focused on hybrid models, standardized benchmarks, and deployment-ready solutions for real-world HPC environments. This review contributes a consolidated perspective to guide the development of sustainable, energy-aware scheduling strategies in HPC

title: Strategic Job Allocation Through Sensor Behavior Analysis Using Random Forest and XGBoost
abstract: Data centers are essential in contemporary computing, yet they form a major contributor of carbon emission because of energy inefficiency. This paper discusses how machine learning algorithms (Random Forest and XGBoost) can be utilized in analyzing sensor metrics as one of the ways of making resource use more efficient. Regression and classification were performed on 20 racks, and sensor performance was quite variable in Rack 3 and 19. The Rack 3 had some of the sensors with high Rsquared values, and the sensors in Rack 19 had low R-squared values, and vice versa. In general, the accuracy of both models was similar, although it could be observed that the variation in sensor behavior in distinct racks was apparent. Such knowledge can be used to make intelligent decisions on the distribution of work and help make data centers sustainable. The future research direction will be to implement these models in simulation systems to enhance real-time decision making and decrease on the harmful impact on the environment.

title: MICHC-NN: An Offline Industrial Control Anomaly Detection Algorithm Based on Maximum Information Coefficient
abstract: The industrial control anomaly detection algorithm effectively monitors and identifies anomalies in industrial control systems, ensuring timely issue detection to maintain system reliability, safety, and regular operation. Researchers often integrate a large number of high-precision, high-sampling-frequency sensors into the system to obtain comprehensive real-time equipment operating data. However, deploying consumer-grade high-performance computing devices in large-scale industrial control systems is often impractical, rendering existing anomaly detection systems unusable in practical environments. Most existing sensor feature selection algorithms are unsuitable for industrial control time series datasets, and some suffer from issues such as a limited reduction in the number of sensors and a decrease in anomaly detection accuracy after reduction. We propose an offline industrial control anomaly detection algorithm based on the Maximum Information Coefficient (MICHC-NN) to address these challenges. We utilize the Maximum Information Coefficient to compute correlations among sensors, addressing the issue of existing feature selection algorithms relying on anomaly labels. Additionally, we introduce a key sensor selection algorithm based on correlation, identifying interrelated sensors in an industrial control system and determining the key sensors most susceptible to system anomalies. These key sensors allow the anomaly detection algorithm to be deployed with a smaller footprint in real industrial control environments. Finally, we employ an autoencoder-decoder model with attention mechanisms to train the anomaly detection network. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed anomaly detection algorithm achieves performance comparable to using all sensors, with a 75\% reduction in the number of sensors employed.

title: Evaluating Software Aging Resistance in Serverless Computing Under Stress Workloads
abstract: Serverless computing abstracts infrastructure management, enabling cost-efficient and scalable application deployment. However, multiple operations can be performed simultaneously, leading to system degradation of resources exhaustion during prolonged executions. This study assesses resource utilization in serverless environments using Knative, testing four OS-container engine configurations (Ubuntu/Docker, Ubuntu/Podman, Debian/Docker, Debian/Podman) under stress workload. Results show Ubuntu paired with Docker achieves optimal resource efficiency, avoids software aging, and maintains consistent performance, making it the most effective configuration for scalable serverless deployments. The absence of progressive degradation in resource metrics underscores serverless architectures' potential to resist software aging through autoscaling. Findings provide actionable insights for optimizing resource management in open-source serverless platforms.

title: Bidirectional Diode-Driven Calibration-Free Mach-Zehnder Switch for Scalable Photonic Circuits
abstract: We demonstrate a calibration-free 2\texttimes2 Mach-Zehnder switch (MZS) and a 4\texttimes4 MZS array that integrates thermally actuated phase shifters with oppositely connected diodes on each arm, enabling bidirectional thermo-optic control via polarity-switched voltage inputs.

title: Energy-Aware HPC Scheduling with LLM-Based Power Prediction
abstract: As the increasing energy consumption of High-Performance Computing (HPC) systems places greater strain on electric grid infrastructure, operational strategies for load balancing become critically important. Energy-aware scheduling offers a promising solution by enabling HPC systems to function as actively managed loads within the energy grid. Despite extensive theoretical research on this strategy, practical implementations and real-system evaluations remain scarce. To bridge this gap, we introduce a systematic approach to developing, evaluating, and implementing energy-aware scheduling without modifications to Slurm's core scheduler. Our method includes a novel mechanism for per-job power prediction based on Large Language Model embeddings of enriched job scripts, coupled with a lightweight, deployable scheduling strategy. Our predictor reduces per-job power MAE by 15\% compared to the current state-of-the-art, and our simulated scheduler shifts 4.0 MWh onto on-site solar without throughput loss. These results demonstrate a clear and practical pathway to production deployment of energy-aware scheduling in HPC.

title: Parallel Data Object Creation: Scalable Metadata Management in Parallel I/O Library
abstract: High-level I/O libraries, such as PnetCDF and HDF5, are commonly used by large-scale scientific applications to perform I/O tasks in parallel. These I/O libraries store the metadata of data objects in files along with their raw data. To ensure metadata consistency during parallel data object creation, they require applications to call the metadata APIs collectively using consistent metadata. Such a requirement can result in an expensive consistency check, as its cost increases with the metadata volume and the number of processes. To address this limitation, we propose a new file header format, which uses partitioned metadata blocks to enable independent data object creation and reduce the objects required for consistency check. Our performance evaluation shows that this new design achieves a scalable performance, cutting data object creation times by up to 196\texttimes when running on 4096 MPI processes to create 5,684,800 data objects in parallel.

title: SlimlO: Lightweight I/O Path Design for Write Isolation in FDP-backed In-Memory Databases
abstract: In-Memory Databases (IMDBs) are widely used with HPC applications to manage transient data, often using snapshot-based per-sistence for backups. Redis, a representative IMDB, employs both snapshot and Write-Ahead Log (WAL) mechanisms, storing data on persistent devices via the traditional kernel I/O path. This method incurs syscall overhead, I/O contention between processes, and SSD garbage collection (GC) delays. To address these issues, we propose Slimio, which adopts I/O passthru to minimize syscall overhead and inter-process I/O interference. Additionally, it lever-ages Flexible Data Placement (FDP) SSDs as backup storage to avoid performance degradation from SSD GC. Experimental results show that Slimio reduces snapshot time by up to 25\%, increases query throughput by up to 30\% during non-snapshot periods, and lowers 99.9\%-ile latency by up to 50\%. Furthermore, it achieves a write amplification factor (WAF) of 1.00, indicating no redundant internal writes, thus extending SSD lifespan.

title: Error Analysis of Globally Distributed Workflow Management System
abstract: The management of data-intensive workflows in globally distributed computing systems, such as those used in high-energy physics, presents significant challenges in scalability, resource allocation, and fault tolerance. Workflow Management Systems (WMS) provide a critical framework for addressing these challenges by automating, monitoring, and optimizing the execution of complex computational tasks across heterogeneous resources. This paper introduces the Production and Distributed Analysis (PanDA) system, a sophisticated WMS developed for the ATLAS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). PanDA is engineered to handle the immense data processing and analysis demands of ATLAS, operating on the Worldwide LHC Computing Grid (WLCG), one of the largest distributed computing infrastructures globally. However, faults or errors frequently occur when distributing and managing workloads on such a globally distributed computing grid. Errors can occur in various form across different sites. To understand and mitigate these errors, analysis is the first step. In this work, we analyze the errors that occurs across the globally distributed grid which will be the stepping stone towards designing effective mitigation strategies.

title: A Cache Interaction Graph for Data Locality Optimization
abstract: Optimizing cache efficiency is critical for mitigating the performance gap between CPUs and memory systems. However, the interaction between application data access patterns and the cache hierarchy complicates debugging cache performance. Existing profiling approaches can identify program performance bottlenecks but leave root-cause diagnosis of cache inefficiencies to programmer expertise. This paper presents an innovative approach that not only precisely captures where cache inefficiencies exist but also helps identify why they occur. Our methodology captures the causal relationship of cache interactions among array variables by tracking cache line evictions, while simultaneously measuring both temporal and spatial locality and classifying cache miss types. We use a new visualization technique (a Cache Interaction Graph), to correlate these metrics with detected interaction patterns to identify root causes and appropriate optimizations. Our Cachegrind extension provides variable-level data locality analysis with acceptable overhead. Our real-world cases demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

title: Data Warehouse Design for Multiple Source Forest Inventory Management and Image Processing
abstract: This research developed a prototype data warehouse to integrate multi-source forestry data for long-term monitoring, management, and sustainability. The data warehouse is intended to accommodate all types of imagery from various platforms, LiDAR point clouds, survey records, and paper documents, with the capability to transform these datasets into machine learning (ML) and deep learning classification and segmentation models. In this study, we pioneered the integration of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery and paper records, testing the merged data on the YOLOv11 model. Paper records improved ground truth, and preliminary results demonstrated notable performance improvements. This research aims to implement a data warehouse (DW) to manage data for a YOLO (You Only Look Once) model, which identifies objects in images. It does this by integrating advanced data processing pipelines. Data are also stored and easily accessible for future use, including comparing current and historical data to understand growth or declining patterns. In addition, the design is used to optimize resource usage. It also scales easily, not affecting other parts of the data warehouse when adding dimension tables or other fields to the fact table. DW performance and estimations for growing workloads are also explored in this paper.

title: Accuracy-Aware Mixed-Precision GPU Auto-Tuning
abstract: Reduced-precision floating-point arithmetic has become increasingly important in GPU applications for AI and HPC, as it can deliver substantial speedups while reducing energy consumption and memory footprint. However, choosing the appropriate data formats brings a challenging tuning problem: precision parameters must be chosen to maximize performance while preserving numerical accuracy. At the same time, GPU kernels typically expose additional tunable optimization parameters, such as block size, tiling strategy, and vector width. The combination of these two kinds of parameters results in a complex trade-off between accuracy and performance, making manual exploration of the resulting design space time-consuming. In this work, we present an accuracy-aware extension to the open-source Kernel Tuner framework, enabling automatic tuning of floating-point precision parameters alongside conventional code-optimization parameters. We evaluate our accuracy-aware tuning solution on both Nvidia and AMD GPUs using a variety of kernels. Our results show speedups of up to \texttimes over double precision, demonstrate how Kernel Tuner's built-in search strategies are effective for accuracy-aware tuning, and show that our approach can be extended to other optimization objectives, such as memory footprint or energy efficiency. Moreover, we highlight that jointly tuning accuracy- and performance-affecting parameters outperforms isolated approaches in finding the best-performing configurations, despite significantly expanding the optimization space. This unified approach enables developers to trade accuracy for throughput systematically, enabling broader adoption of mixed-precision computing in scientific and industrial applications.

title: Energy Aware GPU Kernel Optimization: a Hierarchical Approach
abstract: Graphics Processing Units are crucial for High Performance Computing, but their constantly increasing energy use makes sustainability a problem that is often ignored by traditional performance optimization. This leaves a substantial gap in understanding about the trade-offs between performance and energy. This work presents a structured framework for energy-aware CUDA kernel optimization, incorporating performance, power, and thermal analysis via a six-level hierarchical process and concurrent real-time monitoring, essential for understanding genuine performance-energy efficiency. This framework employs a six-level hierarchical optimization taxonomy, progressing from a naive global memory access baseline to advanced multi-technique integration, including memory coalescing, shared memory tiling, occupancy optimization, and register blocking. This allows precise measurement of each technique's contribution. Real-time energy use is tracked with NVIDIA's Management Library, alongside GFLOPS performance and thermal data to evaluate speed-power trade-offs. Using Dense Matrix-Matrix Multiplication as the test workload, experiments on NVIDIA Tesla V100 and T4 GPUs showed significant gains. Occupancy optimization proves to be the most effective strategy, delivering a 110.9 \% performance improvement on the Tesla V100 and a 57.8 \% speedup on the Tesla T4. These gains are achieved while maintaining power consumption levels comparable to other runs. This work provides quantitative evidence that targeted optimizations can dramatically improve throughput without a corresponding energy penalty, offering clear principles for energy-efficient software development.

title: An architecture for Web-enabled engineering applications based on lightweight high performance CORBA
abstract: Many scientific and engineering computer applications are computationally intensive. These applications are generally hosted on powerful servers, often multi-processor or cluster configurations. Engineers typically login to these servers and launch these applications through shell commands or scripts. When multiple engineering applications need to run in a design experiment flow, a complicated script in languages like PERL is needed. For long-running jobs, the user has to continuously check job status to learn when results can be accessed. Furthermore, special software is needed for a user to remotely login to the computation servers and the user must know on which machine an application of interest resides. This paper describes "Engineering Computing Portal, " an architecture and its implementation for simplifying the use of scientific and engineering applications using Web technology and lightweight high performance CORBA technology.

title: Low-Power Silicon Photonic Modulator for On-Chip Optical Interconnects
abstract: The increasing demand for high-speed and energy efficient data transfer in modern computing systems has driven the adoption of optical interconnects as an alternative to conventional electronic links. In this work, we present a low-power silicon photonic modulator specifically designed for on-chip optical interconnect applications. The proposed device employs a compact Mach–Zehnder interferometer with PN-depletion phase shifters, optimized to achieve a low V\ensuremath\piL product, reduced insertion loss, and high extinction ratio. Through simulations and preliminary measurements, the design demonstrates operation up to 100Gb/s with an energy consumption of less than 0.35pJ/bit, outperforming traditional electronic and photonic baselines. There are also results which demonstrate excellence in bit error rate (BER) operation in forward error correction (FEC) thresholds and better thermal stability than is desired in large-scale integration. This confirms the applicability of the proposed modulator to making it possible to provide scalable, low-latency, and power-effective optical interconnects to next-generation high-performance computing and data center architectures.

title: In-memory Adder Based on Majority Gates with Voltage-Gated Spin-Orbit Torque Magnetoresistive Random Access Memory Devices
abstract: In the study of in-store computation using novel nonvolatile memory arrays, the latency of the in-store adder tends to grow exponentially with the bit width, which seriously affects the computational performance. This paper designs a voltagegated spin-orbit torque magnetoresistive random-access memory (VGSOT-MRAM) cell and proposes a circuit design method for the in-store adder. The proposed series-connected memory cell structure effectively solves the problem of low resistance value of the magnetic memory cell by means of resistive summation; secondly, the proposed in-store computational architecture based on the voltage-regulated spin-orbit-moment magnetic memory cell-crossing array utilizes the 3-input majority decision logic gate realized during the ``read'' operation to further reduce the logic depth of the adder. The depth of the adder logic is further reduced by utilizing a 3-input majority decision logic gate implemented during the ``read'' operation.

title: Advanced Bevel Deposition for Enhanced Yield and Cost Efficiency in Wafer-Level Bonding
abstract: Wafer-level bonding is critical for advanced packaging but often suffers from edge yield loss caused by bubble defects, which originate from uncompensated edge rolloff profiles. Traditional mitigation techniques, such as iterative Tetraethyl Orthosilicate (TEOS) deposition and chemical mechanical polishing (CMP), are resource-intensive, costly, and inflexible. This work introduces two transformative solutions to these challenges: (1) a Predictive Experimental Simulation (PES) methodology that drastically reduces development resource consumption, and (2) an in-situ bevel depositionetching integration within a single Lam Coronus chamber to enhance process capability. Firstly, the PES methodology replaces post-bonding qualitative defect inspection with prebonding quantitative profile evaluation. This three-phase approach includes defining quantitative criteria, computational simulation, and experimental validation, ensuring defect-free bonding by aligning the bevel profile with predefined metrics in a single experimental iteration. This method reduced wafer consumption by 90\% and development time by 70\%. For a hybrid bonding product, the application of bevel deposition reduced CMP cycles from 12 to 2, providing an 80\% cost reduction. Secondly, the in-situ bevel deposition-etching technique combines hardware and process optimization to synthesize precise, complex bevel profiles. The successful creation of a step-shaped profile eliminated edge roll-off and associated defects. This unified approach reduced development costs by 50\% compared to conventional multi-tool methods. For a fusion bonding product, it resulted in a 5\% production yield increase and 50\% reduction in CMP cost. Together, these innovations significantly accelerate wafer bonding process development, enhance robustness, and meet critical scalability demands for future heterogeneous integration.

title: Enhanced Reliability of Large BGA Assemblies for AI Server and HPC Application
abstract: Large ball-grid-array (BGA) packages for artificial intelligence (AI) servers and high-performance computing (HPC) systems face increasing reliability risks due to thermal cycling stress, driven by coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) mismatch and package warpage. The traditional combination of SAC-305 BGA ball and SAC305 solder paste can no longer meet the increasingly stringent reliability requirements. This study evaluates the combined effect of advanced, reliability-enhanced BGA ball alloys: SACA (modified SAC405, containing $\sim 1 \textwt. \% \textBi$, doped with Ni) and SAC-B (modified SAC405, containing $\sim 3 \textwt. \% \textBi$, doped with Ni)) and five contrasting solder pastes: a ductile solder alloy, DFLT (melting temperature is $\sim 206^\circ \mathrmC$, reflowable above 210\textdegree C, selected for its lower reflow temperature to help reduce the warpage), three high-strength alloys (HR1, HR9 and HR12, all with melting temperatures close to SAC305, chosen for their enhanced reliability properties) and SAC305 on solder joint fatigue performance in a $65 \times 65 ~\textmm$ BGA assembly. Thermal cycling tests up to 800 cycles were performed, followed by dye-and-pry inspection and cross-section analysis to quantify crack initiation and propagation. Results show that solder paste selection strongly influences reliability. The SAC-B+DFLT combination exhibited the best performance, with the lowest cracked-joint counts and minimal crack length ratios, while SAC-A+SAC305 showed the highest damage severity. Analysis may indicate that In elements from DFLT lower reflow peak temperature down to $\sim 220 ^\circ \mathrmC$, slow down the cracking formation and control IMC growth. Although more investigation is still ongoing on the strengthening mechanism, this work provides practical insights into alloy-paste synergy for large BGA reliability and introduces a strategy that not only improves thermal fatigue resistance but also reduces warpage, energy consumption and carbon footprint through lower-temperature processing, offering a sustainable solution for next-generation AI and HPC applications.

title: Detection of Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) Attack on EV Charging Station using XGBoost Algorithm
abstract: The growing use of electric vehicles (EV) has accelerated the demand for EV charging infrastructure. However, the emergence of this new world also brings its associated cybersecurity challenges, namely Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack scenarios, which can cause a disturbance in the charging process and lead to operational losses. As few studies have previously investigated lightweight, system-profiling methods with machine learning for real-time DDoS detection, previous works have largely focused on deep learning and network-based intrusion detection methods to protect EV charging stations. This study focuses on building an early detection process for DDoS attacks on Electric Vehicles Charging Station (EVCS) where machine learning method is applied to be useful for early detection. CICEV2023 dataset was selected, it includes many features like EV (Electric Vehicle) and CS (Charging Station) ID and all the events of operating system (OS) and hardware performance counters (HPC). The methodology that was applied includes data preprocessing, feature selection, and training of the XGBoost for the classification model. Model performance evaluation is based upon the metrics of accuracy, precision, recall, and the F1 score. XGBoost has reached 97.20\% accuracy, clearly outclassing Random Forest (89.50\%) and SVM (67.78\%). Such system-level behavioral signatures permit real-time attack detection without requiring network traffic analysis.

title: MobileNet-Lite-Health: A Sustainable Edge AI Framework for Medical Image Classification and Carbon-Aware Computing
abstract: Deep learning has transformed medical image analysis, achieving high accuracy in classification, segmentation, and diagnosis. However, the substantial computational and energy demands of advanced models, such as large convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and multimodal vision-language systems, hinder their deployment on resource-constrained edge devices like smartphones, especially in mobile health. This challenge is critical in low-resource, bandwidth-limited settings with limited high-performance computing access, exacerbating healthcare disparities. This paper introduces MobileNet-Lite-Health (MLH), a lightweight CNN framework optimized via quantization, pruning, and knowledge distillation for sustainable medical imaging inference. We assess MLH on MedMNIST (PathMNIST subset) and HAM10000 datasets, representing benchmark and clinical contexts, respectively. The main contributions of this paper are: 1) a carbon-aware evaluation pipeline integrating CodeCarbon for CO2 tracking and real-time battery profiling on devices like the Google Pixel 6; 2) comparisons with ResNet-18 and MobileNetV2, showing 74\% energy reduction and 76\% CO2 decrease per inference with a 2\% accuracy drop; and 3) scaling simulations projecting approximately 1.1 g annual CO2 savings per clinic for 50,000 screenings. MLH serves as a green alternative to energy-intensive models like GPT-4V and MedPaLM, unsuitable for edge use. Experimental results confirm MLH's effectiveness, with 84.7\% accuracy on PathMNIST and 80.1\% on HAM10000, plus low latency (65 ms) and memory use (95 MB). This work pioneers carbon-aware edge AI, promoting sustainable, accessible healthcare in resource-scarce environments by balancing efficiency, utility, and environmental impact.

title: Multi-Objective Deep Reinforcement Learning with Fuzzy Evolutionary Reward Shaping for Pareto-Optimal Policy Optimization
abstract: Multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) seeks to optimize multiple conflicting goals simultaneously, but conventional fixed-weight scalarization methods often bias learning toward limited regions of the Pareto front. To address this, we propose a novel fuzzy evolutionary reward shaping framework for multi-objective deep reinforcement learning that dynamically adapts scalarization weights to the environmental context. The core idea integrates fuzzy inference with genetic algorithm (GA)-based parameter evolution, enabling adaptive mapping of normalized spatial depth into objective weights that balance treasure collection and time efficiency. The technology leverages deep reinforcement learning agents guided by fuzzy GA-shaped scalarization, contrasted against fixed-weight baselines across 500 episodic experiments. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves robust convergence with an average scalarized return above 15, $\mathrmR^2$ of 0.91, and greater dispersion across the Pareto front, ensuring diverse policy outcomes. Error distributions concentrate in high-return regions, validating the resilience and adaptability of the method. This hybrid fuzzy-evolutionary framework introduces novelty by embedding interpretability and adaptability directly into reward shaping, overcoming static bias. By advancing reliable and adaptive policy optimization, the proposed work can support societal needs in autonomous navigation, robotics, resource allocation, and smart decisionmaking systems, contributing to efficiency and sustainability in real-world environments.

title: An Efficient Multiobjective Optimization Edge Server Deployment Strategy Based on Spectral Clustering and Deep Q-Network
abstract: Edge server deployment is a critical component of mobile edge computing for meeting low-latency requirements while promoting sustainable and energy-efficient operation. Practical deployment is challenging because latency, energy consumption, and load balance are tightly coupled, and the decision space grows rapidly with network scale under time-varying traffic demand. Despite extensive studies, existing approaches often exhibit a scale–adaptivity tradeoff in large-scale scenarios: Scalable placement strategies are typically static under temporal demand variations, whereas adaptive learning-based methods may incur slow convergence or high training cost in high-dimensional deployment spaces. To address this, we propose SC-DQN, a scalable two-stage strategy integrating spectral clustering (SC) and deep Q-network (DQN). SC first partitions base stations using geographic proximity and connectivity information to reduce dimensionality and provide a structured initial deployment. DQN then iteratively refines server placement under dynamic traffic demand, where multiobjective optimization is implemented via a scalarized reward to explicitly control the latency–energy–load tradeoff. Extensive experiments on real-world Shanghai Telecom data demonstrate that SC-DQN achieves improved overall performance compared with representative baselines across multiple scenarios, improving load balancing and reducing latency and energy consumption by up to 28.47\%, 34.82\%, and 7.08\%, respectively.

title: Performance Computing of the Flyback Converter in the Discontinuous Conduction Mode
abstract: In this paper, single switch Flyback converter in discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) of converter operations presents to improve performances when it is nurtured with sustainable high performance computing of design. Optimized design and fabrications of the proposed converter enhances the power circuit efficiency and insight dimension for wide range of the input voltage and load variations when it is assessed by mode wise converter circuit operations. Finally modeling and simulation contribute relevant and important design insights for galvanic version and features of the SMPS applications

title: Scalable Deep Learning for Greenland Ice Bed Topography Prediction
abstract: The rapid evolution of deep learning and GPUaccelerated computing has revolutionized large-scale geospatial modeling, yet the application of these advances to high-resolution ice sheet bed topography prediction remains challenging due to the sheer volume of input data and the computational demands. In this work, we investigate the performance of increasing spatial extents on the Greenland Upernavik dataset through distributed multi-node multi-GPU training pipelines using the BedTopoCNN architecture with the DeepTopoNet framework. Three spatial extents-600\texttimes600, 1200\texttimes1200, and 2400\texttimes2400 pixels are systematically benchmarked on both the Frontera supercomputer and CHIP cluster via PyTorch's Distributed Data Parallel (DDP) framework from single GPU to four nodes with sixteen GPUs total. We measure training throughput, strong scaling efficiency, prediction accuracy, and analyze how larger input patches impact convergence speed, resource utilization, and model fidelity. Our results demonstrate that while the 600\texttimes600 spatial extent dataset delivers optimal training throughput (5.5 hours on four nodes with sixteen GPUs, 73.8 \% time reduction), the 1200\texttimes1200 spatial extent dataset achieves superior prediction quality with training times (9 hours on four nodes with sixteen GPUs, 59\% parallel efficiency). The 2400\texttimes2400 extent initially overwhelmed with BedTopoCNN architectures, but introducing bottleneck layers gives training time of 22 hours (Frontera) and 32 hours (CHIP) on four nodes with sixteen GPUs. This work establishes practical guidelines for deploying distributed training on large geospatial datasets for scaling beyond memoryconstrained regimes, for operational ice sheet modeling and sea level rise projections. The source code for scaling DeepTopoNet and all related experiments is available at: https://github.com/Homayra22/Scalable-Deep-Learning-for-Greenland-Ice-Bed

title: DEPUTY: A DPU-Based Network Offloading Architecture with Minimal CPU Involvement for Stable Network Performance
abstract: The growing demand for High-Performance Computing (HPC) and large-scale AI services has led to a significant increase in workloads that require processing Big Data in real time. While the GPU handles most of the computation, frequent CPU intervention in network processing and data transfer often leads to system performance bottlenecks and inefficient resource utilization. To address this problem, we propose DEPUTY, a system that enables network processing without CPU involvement by offloading all network-related tasks to the Data Processing Unit (DPU). DEPUTY performs all network-related operations on the DPU, including receiving client requests, transferring data to GPU memory, checking GPU inference results, and sending the results back to the client. To achieve this, we utilize DOCA DMA and develop a ring buffer-based data structure in GPU memory, enabling efficient and synchronized data transmission between the DPU and GPU. DEPUTY employs index-based polling to minimize synchronization overhead while ensuring reliable communication. Unlike RDMA, DEPUTY does not require specialized hardware and tightly coupled network configurations on the client side, allowing compatibility with broader deployment environments. Additionally, to minimize CPU overhead during inference, the entire inference workflow is expressed as a CUDA Graph, allowing GPU to autonomously execute kernels in sequence without requiring repeated CPU intervention. Experimental results show that DEPUTY achieves up to $1.96 \times$ higher throughput compared to an existing DPUbased offloading method. Using DEPUTY, it effectively reduces CPU resource consumption and mitigates system performance bottlenecks.

title: High-Performance Computing for Supporting Electric Vehicle Integration into the Transport Industry
abstract: The ongoing energy transition and the rapid electrification of transport increase the importance of integrating renewable energy sources into smart mobility systems. Among these, solar energy plays a central role, but the variability of solar radiation poses significant challenges for planning electric vehicle (EV) charging and ensuring the reliable operation of transport networks. This work addresses these challenges by combining Big Data approaches and High-Performance Computing (HPC) to improve solar radiation forecasting and assess its implications for sustainable transport as a novelty from previous works. A Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network was the focus, and it was trained to predict key meteorological variables - global solar radiation, temperature, and wind speed - using both the original dataset of 13 years and expanded datasets of up to 130 years, generated to simulate Big Data scenarios. Forecasting performance remained stable across datasets, with R2 values above 0.85 for all variables. The best predictive results were obtained for the original dataset, achieving R2 = 0.9884 for solar radiation, while the HPC reduced execution time compared to conventional desktop environments. These results demonstrate that larger datasets improve model scalability and robustness, but significantly increase computational demands. The Deucalion supercomputer achieved the best performance, processing the largest dataset (130 years) in 44.24 minutes, while the same task on a Ryzen 7 required 51.00 minutes. The proposed approach highlights the potential of integrating Big Data and HPC to support EV charging optimisation, smart grid operation, and sustainable mobility strategies, contributing to faster, more reliable, and data-driven decision-making in the energy–transport ecosystem.

title: Optimizing Data-Parallel Workflows for Scientific Computing: Harnessing HPC Resources for Scalable Analytics
abstract: As scientific disciplines become increasingly data-driven, the ability to efficiently handle massive datasets has become critical. This research focuses on optimizing data-parallel workflows on High-Performance Computing (HPC) systems for executing complex, scalable, data-centric applications. The study investigates how dynamic HPC resources can efficiently execute multi-task scientific campaigns using frameworks including Dask, Apache Spark, and RADICAL-Pilot. The primary challenges addressed include workflow distribution across parallel heterogeneous HPC systems, with emphasis on task synchronization, resource allocation, and fault tolerance. Through performance evaluation using molecular dynamics and ecological modeling use cases, this research aims to identify efficient frameworks for large-scale data analytics in scientific computing. The findings are expected to provide insights for maximizing computational efficiency and data throughput in computational science and engineering applications.

title: Microgrid Architecture for AI Computing Facilities
abstract: Hybrid microgrid architectures integrating solar photovoltaic (PV), wind turbines, and battery energy storage systems (BESS) can significantly enhance reliability and sustainability for AI computing facilities, whose energy demands are projected to reach 8\% of global electricity consumption by 2030 [1]. Multi-objective optimization algorithms such as NSGA-II and PSO demonstrate up to 99.6\% renewable energy coverage while optimizing energy allocation and efficiency through balanced resource integration [2] [3]. AI-based controls improve stability and reduce energy waste by 15–20\%, though cybersecurity and integration challenges remain concerns [4].This study presents a simulation-based methodology integrating the Vessim co-simulator and NREL's System Advisor Model (SAM) to evaluate PV–wind–BESS microgrids under AI workloads, using Perlmutter supercomputer data (1.62 MW average). Through multi-horizon optimization, the system achieves \geq95\% renewable coverage while reducing response time by 30.5\%, undershoot by 75.8\%, and steady-state error by 68.7\%. Real-world case studies, such as Microsoft's 100 MW RNG-fueled San Jose microgrid, validate the approach with improved energy reliability over traditional grid-dependent systems. These results demonstrate the feasibility of resilient, efficient power for AI facilities and highlight pathways toward hydrogen integration and scalable adoption.

title: LSTM based DDos Attacks Prevention and Detection for EV Charging Batteries
abstract: Electric Vehicle charging infrastructure is crucial to the sustainable energy transition but it is also susceptible to cyberattacks. Protection against possible cyberattacks, such as Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) assaults, has become crucial with the growth of electric vehicle supply equipment (EVSE) networks. The extensive Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE) dataset, which includes high-performance computing (HPC) statistics, system performance indicators, and network traffic data, is used to analyze the proposed approach, and to create a strong anomaly detection framework by utilising deep learning techniques, to analyse host-based data, such as kernel eventlogs and HPC data. LSTM based model is used for sequence-based learning, analysing high-granularity event sequences to identify anomalous patterns, and putting in place a preprocessing pipeline that guarantees dependable data input for the model are some of the main contributions.

title: ML-Based Detector for Microarchitectural and Side-Channel Attacks on Embedded IoT Devices
abstract: The use of IoT and embedded systems has been rapidly expanding in smart homes, healthcare, and industry, However, these technologies minimal computational and memory resources, lightweight design, and constant connectivity make them extremely vulnerable to side-channel and microarchitectural attacks. Existing countermeasures such as traditional security-based mechanisms can be too resourceheavy, thus reducing efficiency, performance, and increasing power consumption. In this proposed project, we will develop lightweight Machine Learning (ML)-based detectors that can run from the device on low-resource devices to identify and notify attack patterns in real time. The Detector uses simple featuressuch as execution timing, performance counters, and (optional) power bursts analysis using small ML models- Decision trees and lightweight NNs. This framework of detection will provide effective accuracy with very limited memory usage and energy overhead. The neutral design framework and methodology will offer tangible large-scale security expansion to provide practical, cost effective, defendable attack surface detection from cache contention, timing leakage, and covert channel attack detection.

title: A Scalable 64-Bit Hybrid Multiplier Combining Vedic Arithmetic and Wallace Tree Compression
abstract: Innovative developments in the fields of high-performance computing, signal-processing platforms, and autonomous embedded systems have jerked the demand for arithmetic units to be ultra-fast and power-efficient. Multipliers, the most computation-heavy modules in each data path, thus form the major specifications for throughput, latency, and silicon footprint of modern VLSI systems. This innovation has resulted in an optimized 64-bit Hybrid Vedic-Wallace Tree Multiplier synthesizing the computational parallelism of Urdhva tiryagbhyam and efficiency reduction in operand with the Wallace Tree architecture. This hybrid model is characterized by Vedic partial-product generation combined with logarithmic depth compression stages and a high-performance Kogge-Stone final adder. In-depth evaluation using Verilog HDL confirms that the architecture surpasses all conventional architectures-those based on Wallace, UT-based Vedic and Nikhilam in propagation delay, structural regularity and resource efficiency. Including over 4.6 ns of critical-path delay confirms the necessary merits to qualify the design as highly attractive for next-generation DSP accelerators, cryptographic processors, low-latency embedded architectures, and high-frequency FPGA/ASIC implementations. Future extensions will comprise pipelined hybrids, power-aware adaptive multiplier cores, and quantum-ready reversible architectures.

title: Sustainable Data Mining Framework for Regulatory Compliance and Settlement Analytics in Global Financial Markets
abstract: The paper provides a Sustainable Data Mining Framework (SDMF), which is aimed at enhancing regulatory compliance and settlement analytics in world financial markets. The architecture incorporates big data processing, AI-based anomaly detection, and energy-saving computing into a cloud-native architecture. Quantitative experiments were conducted to compare SDMF with conventional systems based on the real time data of financial transactions. This resulted in an increased speed of processing, less use of energy and more accuracy of compliance. The statistical analysis regarding the significance of these gains proved right. It has been shown that sustainability can co-exist with high-computational performance, making regulation transparency and environmental responsibility in the current financial data ecosystem possible.

title: Innovative Thermal Design: How Nature is Redefining Heat Management in Supercomputing
abstract: The urgent need to properly manage thermal conditions of supercomputing systems has become increasingly important because of their rising complexity and performance levels. The three standard cooling techniques that use air cooling fans alongside liquid circuits along with elaborate refrigerant systems prevail yet fail to strike equilibrium between environmental sustainability and operational performance. The deployment of such conventional cooling methods consumes vast amounts of power and results in substantial operational expenses alongside environmental deterioration. A meaningful change has occurred through implementing nature-based cooling solutions during the past few years. Thermal load reduction and energy reduction become achievable through innovative utilization of environmental resources including cold air from outdoor temperatures, ocean water, underground temperatures and glacial environments by organizations today. Several real-life examples prove natural cooling methods effective for large-scale high-performance computing operations: Microsoft uses underwater facilities while Facebook operates in Arctic conditions and Google accesses ocean water for cooling. The study evaluates heat management evolution by studying standard cooling practices against nature-driven heat removal solutions. The research explores ways to use natural elements for improving thermal efficiency while simultaneously reducing operational costs toward creating sustainable computing systems. The paper demonstrates through quantitative assessment and concrete environmental applications that natural elements are effective solutions for supercomputing heat management.

title: The Inevitable Shift to Liquid Cooling in Data Centers
abstract: The accelerating expansion of data centers have heightened the demand for cooling systems that are both efficient and sustainable. This paper examines the performance, safety, and compatibility of three immersion-cooling fluids: a hydrocarbon oil, Thermasolv $ ^\textTM$ CF2 (a fluorinated single-phase fluid), and Thermasolv $ ^\textTM$ IM6 (a fluorinated two-phase fluid). Traditionally, air-cooled systems have had limitations in managing high-density workloads. Air-cooled data centers contribute significantly to energy consumption, water usage, and operational costs. As artificial intelligence (AI), highperformance computing, and hyperscale cloud services expand, two-phase immersion cooling has emerged as a viable alternative. This technology immerses IT hardware in dielectric heat-transfer fluids, allowing for significantly improved thermal management, reduced reliance on mechanical refrigeration, and improved Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE). The favorable characteristics of most dielectric fluids allow for optimal surface contact which contributes to a superior heat transfer performance. Case studies demonstrate that immersion cooling can reduce cooling energy consumption related to air handling systems and pumps by up to 40\% and support rack densities exceeding 100 kW which exceed the limits of air-cooled systems. The need for increased data center capacity has made efficient and sustainable two-phase cooling solutions a critical priority.

title: Smart Farm Productivity Monitoring Model Based on Task Offloading in Edge-Cloud Architecture
abstract: Smart farm productivity monitoring is pivotal for advancing agricultural intelligence, ensuring food security, and promoting sustainable development. To achieve the efficient operation and precise management of smart farms, traditional monitoring solutions, whether cloud-centric or standalone edgebased, suffer from inherent flaws such as excessive latency, inefficient bandwidth utilization, and unbalanced computing resource allocation, failing to meet the real-time and precise demands of modern smart farms. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a smart farm productivity monitoring model based on edge-cloud architecture and enhanced by task offloading. The proposed model leverages the high-performance computing and storage capabilities for performing intensive tasks including model training and global data analysis. Therefore, edge devices are enabled to provide real-time data collection, lightweight preprocessing and low-latency monitoring tasks through offloading prediction task to the network edges. The proposed edge-cloudbased model supports an efficient smart farm monitoring workflow that achieves accurate identification of farm productivity by delivering information to the cloud instead of large-size image data. Therefore, the monitoring is operated by edge layer to derive the information of farm environment. Furthermore, the delivered farm information is used for presenting the real-environment in the cloud layer.

title: Application of Deep Reinforcement Learning in FPGA Multi-Frequency Clock Phase-Shifting Adaptive Measurement
abstract: This paper, in view of traditional FPGA clock frequency phase shift in a dynamic environment adaptive measuring method, precision limited problem, this study proposes a reinforcement learning based on depth (DRL) adaptive measurement algorithm. By constructing a decision-making framework for the interaction between the agent and the environment, a multi-dimensional state space is designed, which includes clock frequency characteristics, phase deviation indicators, environmental interference parameters and system resource states, and a discrete-continuous hybrid action space is determined, such as phase adjustment and measurement strategy selection. As the core, combined with the phase deviation both reward function, resource consumption and environmental interference ResNet and attention mechanism of hybrid neural network is adopted to improve the end-to-end optimization. The experimental results show that compared with traditional method, the DRL will measure precision up to 30 ps, precision is 47\%. At the same time, through the model pruning and knowledge distillation technology, the computing resource consumption is reduced by 63\%. The algorithm in dynamic change frequency clock jitter and + 15 ps environment conditions show the strong robustness, precision measuring equipment for high performance computing and provides a high precision, low utilization of adaptive measuring solution.

title: Extending the Service Life and Enhancing Efficiency of Panel Boards in High-Demand Environments
abstract: SUMMARYThe demand for electrical power is increasing at an unprecedented rate, driven by the explosive growth of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the corresponding rise in high-performance computing workloads. In data centers, this surge is pushing the limits of power consumption, requiring robust and scalable infrastructure to support AI-driven operations.Modern data center power distribution architectures are designed to deliver reliable and redundant power from utility sources through switchgear, UPS systems, and distribution units, ultimately reaching server racks via low-voltage panel boards. These panel boards are critical components that manage and distribute power to both compute systems and auxiliary infrastructure such as liquid cooling systems, including chillers and pumps.As server hardware evolves and current densities increase, panel boards must be engineered to remain resilient under elevated thermal and electrical stresses. While liquid cooling improves energy efficiency at the rack level, panel boards must accommodate the increased power demands of both the servers and the cooling systems.
